tools.name: get_population_snapshot
tools.description:
Latest GDC population snapshot (the weekly 'Friday report'):
    `total_in_gdc_custody` (every GDC bed type, including probation detention
    centers and RSAT), the jail backlog, and the facility-type components.

    The total is the ONLY population figure; the components are parts of it,
    not alternative totals.

tools.name: get_system_statistics
tools.description:
Headline statistics for the Georgia prison system: population,
    mortality, demographics, facility counts, releases and health measures,
    with the update date and data source GPS assembled them from.

tools.name: list_facilities
tools.description:
List Georgia prison facilities with location, operator, security level,
    capacity, population, warden and latest food-safety score.

    Optional filters are applied to the public list after it is fetched:
    facility_type (e.g. 'State Prison', 'Transitional Center', 'County
    Prison'), county, name_contains, and active_only. Responses are paged:
    `limit` (default 25) and `offset`; `next_offset` says where the rest begins.

tools.name: get_facility_staff_roster
tools.description:
Staff headcount and list for one GDC facility, from a GDC-produced roster.

    Answers "how many staff work at X", "how many officers work there", "list the
    staff at X". `slug` is the facility slug, e.g. 'dooly-state-prison' (use
    list_facilities to find it).

    `title` optionally filters by job title. GDC abbreviates heavily: correctional
    officers appear as "Correctional Ofc", clerical staff as "Admin Support" or
    "Admin Assistant". Try both the plain word and the abbreviation.

    ALWAYS report the `observed` date alongside any figure from this tool. A roster
    is a single-day observation, not a statement about who works there today.

    A zero for a role is a finding about the roster rather than missing data: the
    roster holds no nursing, physician or dental titles anywhere in GDC, which is
    consistent with medical staffing being contracted rather than directly employed.
    Do not assert that reason as established fact.

tools.name: get_facility
tools.description:
One facility's full public record plus its most recent state health
    inspection, if GPS has one.

    `slug` is the facility's gps.press slug, e.g. 'macon-state-prison'. Use
    list_facilities to find it.

tools.name: get_parole_statistics
tools.description:
Georgia parole decisions by year — the series GPS assembled from the
    State Board of Pardons and Paroles' own annual reports, with the metric
    definitions and the instruments note that says how they were built.

    `metric` (exact name from the `metrics` list, e.g. 'cases_considered'),
    `from_year` / `to_year` (fiscal years) filter the series. Paged: `limit`
    (default 100 rows) and `offset`.

tools.name: get_ocga_section
tools.description:
Full text of a section of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated from
    GPS's public mirror.

    `section` is the bare citation without the 'O.C.G.A. §' prefix, e.g.
    '9-14-42', '42-5-2', '17-9-4'.

tools.name: get_mortality_data
tools.description:
Deaths in GDC custody since 2020 — yearly and monthly counts, cause-of-
    death breakdown, deaths by facility, facility type, security level and age.

    With no arguments this returns the whole published document plus a list of
    its sections. `section` returns one section by name (e.g. 'YEARLY
    STATISTICS', 'DEATHS BY FACILITY'); `year` filters the yearly and monthly
    lines to that year; `facility_contains` filters the by-facility ranking AND returns that facility's cause-of-death breakdown.
    Filters are matched against the published lines, which is why the matching
    lines are returned verbatim rather than re-tabulated.

tools.name: get_settlements_data
tools.description:
What Georgia has paid to settle prison death and injury claims — the
    'What Georgia Pays' analysis of state settlement records, returned as the
    published markdown.

tools.name: get_contraband_incidents
tools.description:
Incidents from GDC's own published contraband arrest reports (2010-present, ~1,600 incidents,
    including reports that survive only in the Internet Archive; page: gps.press/contraband-data/):
    one row per incident with GDC's wording verbatim, the people as GDC categorised them
    (staff / officer / contract staff / visitor / civilian), the items, whether an arrest was
    reported, and the GDC source URL. Filters: facility slug (e.g. dooly-state-prison), year,
    actor_category (staff | visitor | civilian | officer | gdc_staff | contract_staff),
    item_category (cellphone, tobacco, marijuana, methamphetamine, ...), arrest_made (yes|no|unstated),
    q (text match). Structured rows name staff, officers and contract staff as GDC printed them; other people appear by category and role only. The narrative is GDC's own text.
    Rows are long (a few thousand characters each): per_page defaults to 5 and is capped at 20;
    use `page` to continue and the filters to narrow. `total` is the number of matches.

tools.name: get_contraband_summary
tools.description:
Summaries of GDC's published contraband arrest reports. `by` = year | facility |
    actor-category | role | item-category | stats. Optional facility slug / year filters (not for
    stats). Counts arrests as GDC reported them; GDC's own running tally is not used because it is
    not a consistent series across copies of the same report.

tools.name: get_facebook_posts
tools.description:
What people on Facebook are saying about Georgia's prisons: public posts in the Ga. Prisons Exposed
    group and comments on GPS's own Facebook posts that GPS kept (families, formerly incarcerated people,
    former officers, advocates), newest first, each with its author, date, link and label:
    'first-hand or inside account' (something specific that happened, seen or lived by the author or told
    by someone inside), 'opinion', 'idea for change', or 'news retold'. Filters: q (words), facility (a
    prison name, e.g. "Telfair"), days (default 30, max 365), label (account | opinion | idea | news),
    limit (default 10, max 60). `counts` gives items and people per label for the whole match.
    These are the authors' own views and accounts, never GPS findings: attribute and link every quote.
    Names of people in custody and GDC numbers are removed before the data leaves GPS.

tools.name: get_health_staffing
tools.description:
Medical staffing in Georgia's prisons under the Department of Corrections' contract with Centurion
    of Georgia LLC: the hours the contract's staffing matrix requires vs the hours Centurion reports
    working, by prison, job and month, July-December 2025, plus the workbook's own understaffing-penalty
    calculation. From Centurion's "GA-MED Productive hours compared to Matrix" workbook, produced by GDC
    under an open-records request (R032595-101926, October 2026). No individuals are named.
    level: contract (system totals and quarterly penalty rows) | facility (one entry per prison, lowest
    share of contracted hours first; or one prison) | position (one prison by job, or a job across prisons)
    | matrix (the contracted staffing in force from March 1, 2026, Amendment 4's Exhibit 3.1: every site's
    full-time equivalents, or one site by shift and job).
    facility: a prison slug (dooly-state-prison), id or name fragment ('Walker'). position: e.g. 'RN',
    'LPN', 'NP/PA'. month: YYYY-MM. Read the returned caveats: medical only (not mental health or dental);
    the penalty figures are the workbook's calculation and do not show whether GDC collected them.

tools.name: get_public_records
tools.description:
Open-records requests Georgia Prisoners' Speak made to Georgia agencies under the Georgia Open
    Records Act, published with every document the agency released, so a cited source can be checked.
    Without ref: the list of published requests (reference, title, agency, dates, status, document
    count). With ref (e.g. 'R032544-101826'): the request as sent, the agency's answers and fee
    estimate, and every file with its URL, page count and SHA-256. q searches titles, summaries and
    request text; agency filters by agency or its short name (GDC). Example: ref='R032544-101826' is
    GDC's drone-detection purchase orders (AirWarden, 2017-2025). Reader page: https://gps.press/records/

tools.name: search_public_records
tools.description:
Full-text search INSIDE the documents Georgia agencies released to Georgia Prisoners' Speak under the
    Georgia Open Records Act and GPS has published at https://gps.press/records/ (contracts, purchase orders,
    price lists, inspection reports, policies, staffing matrices and more). Returns each matching file with its
    record, public download URL, number of occurrences and up to three passages with the page they fall on.
    q: words to find (3+ characters, matched as typed, case-insensitive), e.g. "AirWarden", "Medically
    Intensive Infirmary", "per offender per month". ref: limit to one record, e.g. 'R032595-101926'.
    Scanned pages are searched through GPS's OCR text where it exists. Use get_public_records for the
    record itself (request as sent, agency answers, cost, every file).

tools.name: list_historical_series
tools.description:
GPS Historical Data (page: gps.press/historical-data/): the catalog of yearly series on Georgia's
    prisons, 1925-present. Each series is ONE publisher's measure (GDC and Board of Corrections annual
    reports, the Bureau of Justice Statistics, the State Board of Pardons and Paroles, DOJ, the AJC, UCLA
    Law Behind Bars, the GPS mortality registry) with its definition, coverage and caveats. Topics:
    deaths, homicides, suicides, violence, use_of_force, weapons, parole, time_served, lifers, population,
    capacity, budget, escapes, staffing. Never splice two publishers' series into one trend.

tools.name: get_historical_series
tools.description:
One GPS Historical Data series by year: every value with the source's own label, the source
    (publisher, title, page, URL) and the exact quote it was checked against, plus the series'
    definition BREAKS (never read one trend across a break). Get slugs from list_historical_series,
    e.g. deaths-bjs-state-prisons, homicides-gdc-via-doj, los-pct-released-on-parole-gdc,
    population-yearend-gdc-series, deaths-gps-registry (live). CSV: add ?format=csv to the REST URL.
    Values are paged (`limit` default 25, `offset`); narrow with from_year/to_year/category/subgroup.

tools.name: search_historical_data
tools.description:
Find GPS Historical Data series and dated rule changes by words, e.g. "homicide", "parole",
    "life", "AIDS", "population", "90%".

tools.name: get_historical_events
tools.description:
Dated changes to Georgia parole and sentencing rules and the court rulings on them, 1908-present
    (the 1979 guidelines grid, the 1994-95 Sentence Reform Act, the 1998 90% policy, the 2005 Fulton
    order voiding it, the 2006 and 2008 changes, HB 1176 in 2012), each with its source and quote.
    topic = parole | sentencing | court.

tools.name: search_quotes
tools.description:
Search GPS's published quote collection — statements from incarcerated
    people, families, officials and staff that GPS has already published.

    `attribution_type` is 'named' or 'anonymous'. `category` is one of the
    published categories (call with no arguments and read the results, or see
    gps.press). Paginated: page starts at 1, per_page caps at 100.

tools.name: get_length_of_stay
tools.description:
How long people actually serve in Georgia, by offense and year: average
    sentence, years served, percentage of sentence served, share released on
    parole, and the lifer figures — plus the trend summary.

    `offense` is a case-insensitive substring of GDC's offense name (e.g. 'murder',
    'burglary', 'drug'; also the four-digit offense code). With no `offense` the
    all-crimes series is returned. `year` is the calendar year of release (e.g.
    '2023'). Both filter on this server. Rows are newest year first and paged:
    `limit` (default 30) and `offset`; `matched_offenses` lists what `offense`
    matched. `summary_only` returns just the summary block.

tools.name: get_drug_admissions
tools.description:
Admissions to Georgia prisons on drug offenses for the latest published
    report year, broken down by sex, age band and related measures.

tools.name: search_site
tools.description:
Search gps.press — articles, data pages, research library topics and
    facility pages — and get back ranked titles, URLs and summaries.

    This reads the public /find/ results page. GPS publishes no JSON search
    API, so results are parsed out of the rendered page; treat the ranking as
    the site's own and follow each result's URL before citing it.

tools.name: get_gps_guide
tools.description:
GPS's orientation file for AI clients (llms.txt) — READ THIS FIRST.

    Carries the things the data tools cannot: which figure to lead with when two are
    defensible, how to label budget figures, the exact date of the DOJ findings report,
    and the claims GPS has publicly corrected and will not repeat. Roughly 2,000 words.

    The datasets give you accurate numbers. This is what keeps the sentence around the
    number accurate too.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description:
Read any gps.press page as clean Markdown.

    Every page on the site has a Markdown twin at the same URL with `.md` appended;
    this fetches it. Accepts a full URL, a path, or a bare slug — '/vision2027/',
    'vision2027', and the full https URL all work, with or without '.md'.

    Covers articles, data pages, campaign pages and the intelligence briefings
    (intelligence/facility/{slug}, intelligence/issue/{slug}).

    Long pages are truncated; use `offset` and `limit` to page through one. Pair with
    search_site() to find a page, then read it here rather than guessing its contents.

tools.name: list_intelligence
tools.description:
List GPS intelligence briefings — per-facility and per-issue analyses.

    `kind` filters to 'facility' or 'issue'; `contains` filters on the slug.
    Read any of them in full with get_page(), e.g.
    get_page('intelligence/facility/dooly-state-prison').

    Both kinds are discovered from GPS's public intelligence index pages; if the issue
    hub cannot be read, `issues_note` says so in the payload.
